question: What fish-related material does the 2005 Manila Third Sewerage Project EIS actually report for NCR and adjacent/shared waters, and can any of it support a dated site-level species record?
lineageNote: The 2018 DPWH Phase IV Supplemental EIS cites the Manila Third Sewerage Project EIS as older context; the 2005 source was independently reviewed here.

source.citation: Manila Water Company, Inc. (2005). Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for Manila Third Sewerage Project, Volume 1: Main Text and Figures. February 11, 2005 (Revised Draft). World Bank document E1288 v1.
source.titleAsPublished: Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for Manila Third Sewerage Project, Volume 1: Main Text and Figures
sourceLocators: Printed p. 8 (PDF p. 60): describes an aquatic ecology survey intended to characterize river systems and other water bodies that may be affected by proposed treatment plants; says samples were collected near proposed development locations.
Printed p. 9 (PDF p. 61): East Avenue Station 3 tentative small-fish observation and Pasig River narrative fish context.
Printed p. 10 (PDF p. 62): Marikina River, Taguig River systems in Laguna Lake, Pinagsama Village Creek and East Manggahan Floodway narrative context.
source.accessMethod: Retrieved the World Bank-hosted PDF on 2026-11-24, extracted text, and visually inspected the cover and printed pages 9-10. The 23,038,365-byte temporary PDF and rendered page previews were used only for this review and are not repository assets.
source.reuseNotes: The cover carries a Public Disclosure Authorized marking. No item-specific open license or derived-data redistribution terms were found in the reviewed document. Public disclosure is not treated as a reuse license.

surveyContext.aquaticSurveyPurposeAsReported: Determine the present ecological state of river systems and other water bodies that may be affected by proposed sewage treatment plants; samples were collected near proposed development locations.
surveyContext.fishSpecificDesign: The reviewed fish section supplies no fish-specific sampling date, capture method, effort, sample counts, station-to-species matrix, voucher/catalogue identifiers, or independently inspectable identification material. The broad aquatic-ecology survey statement is not enough to assign those details to the fish lists.
surveyContext.scopeCaution: This EIS combines proposed project sites, regional narrative, reported fishery context, and shared or adjacent waters. It is not a unified NCR fish survey or a current inventory.

waterbodyContexts.areaContextAsReported: East Avenue, Quezon City context in the EIS
waterbodyContexts.observationAsReported: Researchers observed numerous small fish, probably gambuasia or mosquito fish (locally known as kataba).
waterbodyContexts.limitation: The source itself says probably and records no diagnostic evidence. Preserve the printed form gambuasia; do not normalize it to Gambusia or admit a species occurrence.

waterbodyContexts.areaContextAsReported: Regional river narrative; no sampled reach or NCR station is linked to the fish labels
waterbodyContexts.dominanceClaimAsReported: Janitor fish, identified in the text as Hypostomus plecostomus, was apparently the most abundant; the other listed fish stocks are described as reportedly present.
waterbodyContexts.sourceInterpretationAsReported: The EIS describes the resources as pollution-tolerant, flushed down from Laguna Lake or Marikina River, and transient in more polluted reaches of the main waterways.
waterbodyContexts.limitation: No fish-specific event, collection date, reach, count, method, voucher, or taxon-to-station link is supplied. The source's movement and transient-population interpretation is not independently validated here.

waterbodyContexts.areaContextAsReported: The EIS says janitor fish was common and abundant in all parts of the river; its project/survey reach is not given in the fish passage.
waterbodyContexts.commonNameClaimAsReported: Janitor fish was described as the most common and abundant aquatic life; the source did not provide a voucher-linked scientific name for this Marikina statement.
waterbodyContexts.fisheryContextAsReported: The river system was described as supporting sustenance fishing, with harvestable fish dependent on seasonal rainfall and mainly used for family consumption.
waterbodyContexts.limitation: These are not a dated fish-by-site survey table. Preserve the source spellings, including Arias macrocephalus, without silently correcting or cross-linking labels.

waterbodyContexts.waterbodyLabelAsReported: Taguig River systems in Laguna Lake
waterbodyContexts.areaContextAsReported: The text describes fishing along shore areas of Taguig River systems in the lake; Laguna de Bay is shared across NCR and CALABARZON.
waterbodyContexts.limitation: The list is not partitioned by river, shoreline locality, survey event, or NCR side of the lake. Preserve the EIS spellings, including Glossogobious guirus and Ophiocephalus striatus.

waterbodyContexts.areaContextAsReported: The EIS does not state a fish-specific station, date, or survey method in the reviewed sentence.
waterbodyContexts.claimAsReported: Fish habitation is non-existent in the creek.
waterbodyContexts.limitation: This single historical sentence lacks fish-specific sampling details and is not evidence of biological absence, current condition, or a completed coverage check.

waterbodyContexts.areaContextAsReported: Taytay, Rizal context; outside NCR and retained here as a cross-region CALABARZON lead.
waterbodyContexts.commonNameClaimAsReported: Janitor fish was also present at the floodway.
waterbodyContexts.fisheryContextAsReported: The EIS reports local recreational or consumption fishing and says hook-and-line was commonly used for the listed fish; shrimp was also reported in subsistence catches.
waterbodyContexts.limitation: The fish list is not tied to dated capture events, counts, individual stations, or vouchers. No NCR locality is inferred from the Taytay label.

rightsAndEvidenceDecision.decision: Keep the EIS fish labels and statements as attributed research-only leads. Do not treat narrative lists, uncertain names, historical fishery context, or source-reported absence wording as validated occurrences, current presence, a complete checklist, geometry, catchability, safety, or legal fishing guidance.

nextActions: Seek date-, method-, locality-, and taxon-resolved primary fish survey material for Pasig and Marikina River reaches; keep the 2005 EIS context separate from the 2014 Marikina Bridge event.
Search for event-level sources for Taguig River systems and East Manggahan Floodway, preserving Laguna de Bay and Taytay cross-region scope instead of assigning them to NCR alone.
Check exact nomenclature only after the source labels and study contexts have been kept verbatim; no source-name normalization is performed in this review.
Continue NCR and CALABARZON freshwater, brackish, marine, and wetland coverage reviews; this regional EIS screen closes no baseline or waterbody scope.
